title: Port scope and work split
summary: Measured scope of the Lineage 2 Interlude browser client port: client data versus server data, content inventory, layered parts, stage A and stage B work order, and agent allocation.
notes: MANIFEST_TYPE PRD and MANIFEST_PRECEDENCE 1 applied as authoritative. Owner decisions and work-order statements recorded for synthesizer conflict detection. Section 'Owner decisions, 2026-11-07': (1) 'First goal: a working browser client with every client asset converted.' (2) 'The server is replaceable. Stock L2J Mobius is the first target. If it does not work out, the game moves to SpacetimeDB...' (3) 'Because of 2, the client never computes gameplay outcomes. It displays what a server sends.' Section '6. Order of work': 'Stage A converts the whole client and proves it in the offline sandbox' before 'Stage B plugs in a server through GameWorldAdapter'. Stage A order: 1 decode all 40 .dat tables and fix the sysstring/systemmsg count; 2 batch-convert all 153 tiles; 3 all player characters, every race, gender and class; 4 NPCs and monsters; 5 skill visuals and sounds; 6 UI windows. Stage B order: 1 Mobius adapter login, character select, world entry, then event dispatch; 2 combat, dialogs, shops, social and quest windows; 3 SpacetimeDB adapter only if Mobius does not fit. Section '7': 'Commit first.' and the five GameWorldAdapter methods 'stay frozen'. Section '8': phase table of agent counts, steady state 6 with ceiling 7; 'One agent per part (19) would produce more branches than one person can review.' Section '5' lists 19 parts; part 6 state reads '1 (Greater Musveren)'. Document also contains judgement statements (for example the Auto0 to Auto5 maps are unchecked, and the recommended dumb relay is 'not yet decided').
